title: Brisbane Trivia Night

questions.q: Brisbane takes its name from Sir Thomas Brisbane. Which colonial office did he hold?
What is the name of the steel cantilever bridge that crosses the river to Kangaroo Point?
Which Brisbane NRL club, founded in 1987, is named after a wild horse?
In State of Origin, the Queensland side is known by what colour?
The cricket ground known as the Gabba takes its nickname from which suburb?
Brisbane hosted the Commonwealth Games in which year?
South Bank Parklands was built on the site of which 1988 event?
Which animated series about a family of dogs is set in Brisbane?
Which band of brothers spent part of their childhood in Redcliffe, where a walkway now honours them?
The Moreton Bay bug, a local favourite on the plate, is a type of what?

notes: Named for Sir Thomas Brisbane, Governor of NSW 1821 to 1825; see Brisbane on Wikipedia or the Queensland State Archives.
Story Bridge, opened 1940, links Fortitude Valley and Kangaroo Point; see Story Bridge on Wikipedia or Brisbane City Council.
Brisbane Broncos; the Dolphins (2023) also play in Brisbane, hence the clues.
Queensland Maroons; see State of Origin on Wikipedia or nrl.com.
Brisbane Cricket Ground is in Woolloongabba, hence 'the Gabba'; see thegabba.com.au.
XII Commonwealth Games, Brisbane, 1982; see thecgf.com or Wikipedia.
South Bank Parklands opened 1992 on the former World Expo 88 site; see visit.southbank.com.au or Wikipedia.
Bluey (ABC Kids, Ludo Studio) is set and made in Brisbane; see Bluey (TV series) on Wikipedia.
The Gibb brothers lived in Redcliffe from 1958; Bee Gees Way opened there in 2013; see Redcliffe on Wikipedia or visitmoretonbayregion.com.au.
Moreton Bay bug (Thenus orientalis) is a slipper lobster; see Thenus orientalis on Wikipedia or the Queensland Government fisheries pages.
